answer: Shared-Resource Attestation Windows. Agents must collectively fund a rotating public resource (a compute harbor) each window; identities that repeatedly co-appear in the same funding cluster pay a superlinear share of the next window's cost. An attacker can't harbor many cheap identities without their cluster's rising levy exposing them. Legitimate agents spread across a grove of independent clusters and pay near-baseline. At each dawn the levy resets, so costs track sustained coordination, not one-off registration.
